title: Expose bounded event-type paging from the public store
description:
SPIDR prerequisite 2 of 2 for task-16d5bc3a10864351adf5be10dfa7df00. Hard dependency: task-d20ffd0775b4420bb2318c79019b4127 must be DONE and committed so the v5 `(event_type, global_position)` index is real before this API promises an indexed path.

Fresh measurement at HEAD 6ca5da07: the public `SqliteEventStore`/`DecisionLedgerCore`/`EventReadModelStore` chain exposes aggregate paging and global paging only. The event rows already carry `eventType`, but daemon callers must currently fetch and decode every global event to select one type. The authoritative design requires type filters on the event API, and task-16d5 must preserve cross-aggregate uniqueness, so the minimum reusable store surface is a type-filtered global cursor page—not a daemon-specific effect query.

Deliverable: publish `SqliteEventStore.readEventsByTypeAfter(eventType, afterGlobalPosition, limit?, maxDecodedBytes?)` through the existing store read layers and bare `@moe/store` root. It returns `CursorPage<StoredEvent, bigint>` containing only exact event-type matches in strictly increasing global position, uses the same single-snapshot two-phase candidate/materialization and decoded-byte budget rules as `readEventsAfter`, and is backed by the v5 composite index. This task owns the reusable store query only. Consumer/final hardening task: task-16d5bc3a10864351adf5be10dfa7df00 will call it for `EffectActivationCommitted` and prove the preserved ambiguity invariant.

Owned paths: `packages/store/src/event-read-query.ts`, `event-read-model.ts`, `decision-ledger.ts`, `sqlite-event-store.ts`, and `event-read-model-contract.test.ts`. Verification: `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm verify:store && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`; every test leg must report a nonzero count.
definitionOfDone: The public bare-root `SqliteEventStore` exposes the exact bounded `readEventsByTypeAfter(eventType, afterGlobalPosition, limit?, maxDecodedBytes?)` method and returns the existing `CursorPage<StoredEvent, bigint>` contract without adding a daemon-specific store type.

Across interleaved event types, paging returns only exact matches in strictly increasing global position with no duplicate or skipped matching row; `hasMore` and `nextCursor` are computed over the filtered stream, and literal nonzero page/case counts prevent a vacuous sweep.

Candidate selection and materialization run in one read snapshot, enforce the same `limit + 1` preflight and decoded-byte budget as global paging, and use parameterized SQL over the v5 `(event_type, global_position)` index.

Hostile/empty/oversized event types, invalid cursors/limits/byte budgets, an oversized first matching row, storage corruption, and snapshot faults fail closed with the exact existing durable store code; an unknown but valid event type returns an honest empty page.

A temporary compiled probe inside `apps/daemon` imports `SqliteEventStore` and `CursorPage` from the bare `@moe/store` specifier, typechecks a call to `readEventsByTypeAfter`, and is deleted in the same command; the daemon manifest and lock importer links remain present. The named production consumer is task-16d5bc3a10864351adf5be10dfa7df00.

A production mutation that drops the type predicate or delegates to unfiltered global paging makes a named interleaving test red on exact returned event IDs/count, is confirmed applied, and is restored byte-exact; fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm verify:store && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` exits 0 with nonzero test counts.
taskRails: Do not expose raw DatabaseSync, daemon activation vocabulary, payload JSON paths, caller SQL, or an unbounded array. This is a generic store-owned exact event-type cursor query.
Reuse production input validation, snapshot, decoded-byte budget, row decoding, and cursor assertions. Do not copy a simplified test-only pager or silently normalize invalid event types.
The query must be index-backed by task-d20ffd0775b4420bb2318c79019b4127. A filtered API implemented as a full `SCAN domain_events` does not satisfy this task.
Preserve all global/aggregate paging behavior and public signatures. Assert exact stable store codes on rejection paths and literal positive counts for generated/interleaved cases.
Touch and commit only the five owned paths; preserve foreign WIP. Shared public store changes require the full store and repo regression named above.

implementationPlan.description: RED (TDD). In event-read-model-contract.test.ts add the failing contract suite for readEventsByTypeAfter. Seed a store with INTERLEAVED event types (at least 3 distinct types round-robin across >= 25 events so matching rows are non-adjacent in global_position) and assert: exact returned eventIds and a LITERAL non-zero count per page; strictly increasing globalPosition; no duplicate or skipped matching row across a full multi-page walk driven by nextCursor; hasMore/nextCursor computed over the FILTERED stream (a page whose filtered remainder is empty must report hasMore false even though unfiltered rows remain). Assert the interleaving fixture actually generated the mixed types (literal count of each type) so the sweep cannot pass vacuously. Add an unknown-but-valid event type case asserting an honest empty page (items [], hasMore false, nextCursor null) rather than a throw.
implementationPlan.note: RED. Added the interleaved contract suite. Fixture seedMixed commits 27 events round-robin across 3 types onto aggregate goal-mixed, landing at global positions 4..30 so alpha matches sit at 4,7,10,...,28 — never adjacent. typeTally() reads back through the production readEventsAfter surface and the test asserts the literal generated census {alpha 9, beta 9, gamma 9, contract-1/2/3 1 each}, so the sweep cannot pass vacuously. The walk is driven by nextCursor and asserts literal per-page counts [4,4,1], exact eventIds (event-mixed-0,3,...,24), exact globalPositions 4+3k, Set size 9 (no duplicate/skip), and every item's eventType === alpha. Filtered-stream hasMore is pinned specifically: the last matching row is position 28 while readEventsAfter(28n,10) still returns 2 unfiltered rows, and the page must still report hasMore false / nextCursor 28n; a further call returns the honest empty page. Unknown-but-valid type "goal.absent" returns {items: [], hasMore: false, nextCursor: null} rather than throwing. RED verified: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck exits 1 with TS2551 "Property 'readEventsByTypeAfter' does not exist on type 'SqliteEventStore'" at 24 call sites plus TS2305 for the two not-yet-exported SQL constants.

implementationPlan.description: RED (TDD), rejection paths. Still in event-read-model-contract.test.ts, add cases pinning the EXACT existing stable codes, not merely 'threw': hostile/empty/oversized/NUL/ill-formed eventType -> DurableStoreError code STORE_INPUT_INVALID (thrown by requireIdentifier -> invalidInput at store-input-primitives.ts:17); invalid afterGlobalPosition (negative/non-bigint) -> STORE_INPUT_INVALID via requireNonnegativeBigInt; invalid limit and invalid maxDecodedBytes -> the exact code requirePageLimit / requirePageDecodedByteLimit already raise (read them and pin the literal, do not assume STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED). Include an oversized FIRST matching row case proving the decoded-byte budget refuses rather than returning a partial page. Where two layers could refuse, assert which layer did.
implementationPlan.note: RED, rejection paths. Codes were READ from source, not assumed. store-input-primitives.ts: requireIdentifier:24 -> invalidInput:17 -> STORE_INPUT_INVALID; requireNonnegativeBigInt:54 -> STORE_INPUT_INVALID; requirePageLimit:61 delegates to requireSafePositiveInteger (STORE_INPUT_INVALID "limit must be a positive safe integer") and only crosses to limitExceeded:20 -> STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED "limit cannot exceed 1000" above MAX_PAGE_SIZE. read-page-budget.ts requirePageDecodedByteLimit:22 splits the same way for maxDecodedBytes. So invalid limit/bytes are STORE_INPUT_INVALID, not STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED — the plan's warning was correct and is now pinned literally. Eleven rows added to the existing INVALID_READS table, each asserting DurableStoreError instance + exact code + exact full message: empty/NUL/513-byte/lone-surrogate/non-string eventType -> STORE_INPUT_INVALID `eventType must be well-formed, ...`; -1n and non-bigint cursor -> STORE_INPUT_INVALID afterGlobalPosition; limit 0 -> INVALID, 1001 -> EXCEEDED; bytes 0 -> INVALID, MAX+1 -> EXCEEDED. WHICH-LAYER is pinned: the cursor rows pass a valid eventType with limit 0 and bytes 0 also invalid, so a green assertion proves the cursor validator answered before the limit/byte validators. Oversized FIRST matching row: readEventsByTypeAfter(alpha, 0n, 10, 1) must raise STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED "the next record does not fit within 1 decoded bytes" (selectReadPagePrefix:92 with selected.length === 0) rather than return a partial page; paired with readEventsByTypeAfter("goal.absent", 0n, 10, 1) returning an empty page under the identical budget, which proves the refusal is driven by a row the TYPE FILTER admitted, not by the budget alone.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN. In event-read-query.ts add `protected eventTypePage(eventType, afterGlobalPosition, limit = 100, maxDecodedBytes = MAX_PAGE_DECODED_BYTES): CursorPage<StoredEvent, bigint>`, modeled line-for-line on the existing globalEventPage (lines 101-159). Reuse the production validators ALREADY imported in this file: requireIdentifier for eventType (the same one the write path uses at store-input-commit.ts:151 - do not add a new or laxer string check and do not normalize/trim), requireNonnegativeBigInt, requirePageLimit, requirePageDecodedByteLimit. Keep the whole operation inside ONE this.readSnapshotOperation("read events by type", ...) with this.assertCachedProjectBinding(), the limit + 1 candidate preflight, selectReadPagePrefix, and assertReadPageCursors. Do NOT add a new public store type.

GREEN, the correctness crux. In BOTH SQL phases of eventTypePage carry the type predicate as a bound parameter: candidate phase `WHERE events.event_type = ? AND events.global_position > ? ORDER BY events.global_position LIMIT ?`, and materialization phase `WHERE events.event_type = ? AND events.global_position > ? AND events.global_position <= ? ORDER BY events.global_position LIMIT ?`. Omitting the predicate from the SECOND phase is the specific defect this task must not ship - it would materialize non-matching rows inside the position window and desync assertReadPageCursors. All values bound as parameters; no string interpolation of caller input into SQL.

Wire the three existing read layers, preserving every current signature. event-read-model.ts: add `public readEventsByTypeAfter(eventType, afterGlobalPosition, limit?, maxDecodedBytes?)` delegating to this.eventTypePage. decision-ledger.ts: add the readonly member to the DecisionLedgerCore interface (beside readEventsAfter at ~line 71) and the corresponding delegate in the factory (~line 135). sqlite-event-store.ts: add the thin public delegate `return this.#core.readEventsByTypeAfter(...)` beside readEventsAfter (~line 342) - delegation only, no logic in this file, which is already 372 lines against the 400 hard split. Confirm CursorPage and SqliteEventStore remain exported from the bare @moe/store root barrel.

Prove the query is INDEX-BACKED (task rail 3). Add an assertion in event-read-model-contract.test.ts that EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for the eventTypePage candidate SQL names domain_events_event_type_position and that the plan contains NO `SCAN domain_events`. Pin the plan against the production schema built by the manifest, never a test-created index. If the STORED_EVENT_DECISION_JOIN causes SQLite to prefer another index or a temp b-tree for ORDER BY, that is a real finding: report it rather than weakening the assertion to a substring match.

Prove the bare-specifier consumer edge (DoD 5). Verified already present at planning time: apps/daemon/package.json:22 declares "@moe/store": "workspace:*" and pnpm-lock.yaml carries the apps/daemon importer, so NO manifest edit and no workspace install is needed and neither file is an owned path. Create a TEMPORARY probe file inside apps/daemon that imports { SqliteEventStore } and type { CursorPage } from the BARE "@moe/store" specifier and typechecks a readEventsByTypeAfter call assigned to CursorPage<StoredEvent, bigint>; run the daemon typecheck and DELETE the probe in the same command so no probe file can survive into a commit.

Single verification gate, then the adversarial drill. Run exactly: export PATH="/tmp/moe-node24-bin:$PATH" && pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm verify:store && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test — the PATH prefix is REQUIRED (a bare shell has node 18.19.1 and no pnpm). Read each leg's OUTPUT, not its exit code: record the literal `Test Files N passed` count line per leg; an exit-0 leg with no count line is UNVERIFIED. Then the mutation drill: delete the event_type predicate from the materialization phase (and separately, make readEventsByTypeAfter delegate to globalEventPage), confirm the named interleaving test goes RED on exact returned eventIds/count, restore byte-exact, and re-run the gate. Repo-wide legs are a path-attributed baseline: record failures at merge-base vs HEAD and report any foreign red verbatim - note that 4 of the 5 owned paths currently carry foreign readEventHorizon WIP.
